section.header: United States Naval Community College

subsection.text: Chapter 859 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section:

section.header: United States Naval Community College: establishment and degree granting authority

subsection.text: There is a United States Naval Community College. The primary function of such College shall be to provide—

paragraph.text: programs of academic instruction and professional and technical education for individuals described in subsection (b) in—

subparagraph.text: academic and technical fields of the liberal arts and sciences which are relevant to the current and future needs of the Navy and Marine Corps; and
their practical duties;

paragraph.text: remedial, developmental, or continuing education programs, as prescribed by the Secretary of the Navy, which are necessary to support, maintain, or extend programs under paragraph (1);
support and advisement services for individuals pursuing such programs; and
continuous monitoring of the progress of such individuals.

subsection.text: Subject to such other eligibility requirements as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe, the following individuals are eligible to participate in programs and services under subsection (a):

paragraph.text: Enlisted members of the Navy and Marine Corps.
Officers of the Navy and Marine Corps who hold a commission but have not completed a postsecondary degree.
Civilian employees of the Department of the Navy.
Other individuals, as determined by the Secretary of the Navy, so long as access to programs and services under subsection (a) by such individuals is—

subparagraph.text: in alignment with the mission of the United States Naval Community College; and
determined to support the mission or needs of the Department of the Navy.

paragraph.text: Under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Navy, the head of the United States Naval Community College may, upon the recommendation of the directors and faculty of the College, confer appropriate degrees or academic credentials upon graduates who meet the degree or credential requirements.
A degree or credential may not be conferred under this subsection unless—

subparagraph.text: the Secretary of Education has recommended approval of the degree or credential in accordance with the Federal Policy Governing Granting of Academic Degrees by Federal Agencies; and

the United States Naval Community College is accredited by the appropriate civilian academic accrediting agency or organization to award the degree or credential, as determined by the Secretary of Education.

When seeking to establish degree or credential granting authority under this subsection, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives—

clause.text: a copy of the self assessment questionnaire required by the Federal Policy Governing Granting of Academic Degrees by Federal Agencies, at the time the assessment is submitted to the Department of Education’s National Advisory Committee on Institutional Quality and Integrity; and
the subsequent recommendations and rationale of the Secretary of Education regarding the establishment of the degree or credential granting authority.

subparagraph.text: Upon any modification or redesignation of existing degree or credential granting authority, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a report containing the rationale for the proposed modification or redesignation and any subsequent recommendation of the Secretary of Education on the proposed modification or redesignation.

The Secretary of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a report containing an explanation of any action by the appropriate academic accrediting agency or organization not to accredit the United States Naval Community College to award any new or existing degree or credential.

paragraph.text: The Secretary of the Navy may employ as many civilians as professors, instructors, and lecturers at the United States Naval Community College as the Secretary considers necessary.
The compensation of persons employed under this subsection shall be prescribed by the Secretary of the Navy.

subsection.text: The table of sections at the beginning of chapter 859 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new item:

toc.toc-entry: 8595. United States Naval Community College: establishment and degree granting authority.

section.header: Codification of establishment of United States Air Force Institute of Technology

subsection.text: Chapter 951 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting before section 9414 the following new section:

section.header: United States Air Force Institute of Technology: establishment
section.text: There is in the Department of the Air Force a United States Air Force Institute of Technology, the purposes of which are to perform research and to provide, to members of the Air Force and Space Force (including the reserve components) and civilian employees of such Department, advanced instruction and technical education regarding their duties.

subsection.text: The table of sections at the beginning of such chapter is amended by inserting, before the item relating to section 9414, the following new item:

toc.toc-entry: 9413. United States Air Force Institute of Technology: establishment.

section.header: Clarifications regarding scope of employment and reemployment rights of members of the uniformed services

subsection.header: Clarification regarding definition of rights and benefits
subsection.text: Section 4303(2) of title 38, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.text: by inserting (A) before The term; and
by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:

subparagraph.text: Any procedural protections or provisions set forth in this chapter shall also be considered a right or benefit subject to the protection of this chapter.

subsection.header: Clarification regarding relation to other law and plans for agreements
subsection.text: Section 4302 of such title is amended by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: Pursuant to this section and the procedural rights afforded by subchapter III of this chapter, any agreement to arbitrate a claim under this chapter is unenforceable, unless all parties consent to arbitration after a complaint on the specific claim has been filed in court or with the Merit Systems Protection Board and all parties knowingly and voluntarily consent to have that particular claim subjected to arbitration.

For purposes of this subsection, consent shall not be considered voluntary when a person is required to agree to arbitrate an action, complaint, or claim alleging a violation of this chapter as a condition of future or continued employment, advancement in employment, or receipt of any right or benefit of employment.

section.header: Clarification and expansion of prohibition on gender-segregated training in the Marine Corps
section.text: Section 565 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 (10 U.S.C. 8431 note prec.) is amended—

paragraph.text: in the heading, by inserting and Officer Candidates School after Depots;
in subsection (a)(1)—

subparagraph.text: by striking training and inserting no training platoon ; and
by striking not;

paragraph.text: in subsection (b)(1)—

subparagraph.text: by striking training and inserting no training platoon ; and
by striking not; and

paragraph.text: by adding at the end the following new subsections:

subsection.text: No training platoon at a Marine Corps recruit depot established after the date of the enactment of this Act may be segregated based on gender.

paragraph.text: Subject to paragraph (2), training at Officer Candidates School, Quantico, Virginia, may not be segregated based on gender.
The Commandant of the Marine Corps shall carry out this subsection not later than five years after the date of the enactment of this Act.

section.header: Requirement to issue regulations ensuring certain parental guardianship rights of cadets and midshipmen

paragraph.text: Each Secretary concerned shall prescribe by regulation policies ensuring that the parental guardianship rights of cadets and midshipmen are protected consistent with individual and academic responsibilities.
The regulations prescribed under paragraph (1) shall provide that—

subparagraph.text: a cadet or midshipman of a covered service academy may not be required to give up such cadet or midshipman’s parental guardianship rights in the event of a pregnancy occurring after the beginning of such cadet or midshipman's first day of academic courses;

except as provided under paragraph (3), a covered service academy may not involuntarily dis-enroll a cadet or midshipman who becomes pregnant or fathers a child while enrolled at such academy after the first day of academic courses; and

a cadet or midshipman who becomes pregnant or fathers a child while enrolled at a covered service academy shall be allowed to take leave for up to one year and return to the academy to resume classes afterward.

paragraph.header: Responsibilities of parents enrolled at covered service academies
paragraph.text: The regulations prescribed under paragraph (1) shall require cadets and midshipmen with dependents to establish a family care plan in consultation with and approved by appropriate academy leadership. The family care plan shall—

subparagraph.text: designate a full-time care provider, such as another parent or guardian of the dependent or a family member of the cadet or midshipman, who shall—

clause.text: be responsible for the dependent;
not be enrolled at a covered service academy; and

have either full power-of-attorney or guardianship rights in order to prevent situations where such cadet or midshipman is pulled away from such cadet or midshipman’s duties and responsibilities at the covered service academy;

subparagraph.text: ensure that such cadet or midshipman—

clause.text: does not rely on base facilities or child-care services and is able to function as any other cadet or midshipman, including residing in covered service academy dormitories;

except as provided under paragraphs (4) and (5)(B)(i), does not receive additional compensation benefits or concessions from the covered service academy on account of having a dependent, including money, leave, or liberty;
is not be excused on account of such dependent from standard classes, training, traveling, fitness requirements, or any other responsibilities inherent to attending a covered service academy; and

subparagraph.text: ensure, that if both parents of a dependent are cadets or midshipmen at a covered service academy, the parents shall agree on the family care plan or face expulsion (with no incurred obligations).

paragraph.header: Options for pregnant cadets and midshipmen
paragraph.text: The regulations prescribed under paragraph (1) shall provide that females becoming pregnant while enrolled at a covered service academy shall have, at a minimum, the following options:

subparagraph.text: At the conclusion of the current semester or when otherwise deemed medically appropriate, taking leave from the covered service academy for up to one year followed by a return to full cadet or midshipman status.
Seek a transfer to a university with a Reserve Officers’ Training Corps for the Armed Force under the military department concerned.
Full release from the covered service academy and any related obligations.
Enlistment in active-duty service, with all of the attendant benefits.

paragraph.header: Treatment of males fathering a child while enrolled at covered service academies
paragraph.text: The regulations prescribed under paragraph (1) shall provide that males fathering a child while enrolled at a covered service academy—

subparagraph.text: shall not be required to give up parental rights; and
shall not acquire any benefits or leave considerations as a result of fathering a child, except that—

clause.text: academy leadership shall establish policies to allow cadets and midshipmen at least one week of leave to attend the birth of such child, which must be used in conjunction with the birth; and

in the event the male father becomes the sole financial provider for a dependent, the academy shall provide the father the same options available to a cadet or midshipman who becomes a mother while enrolled, including remaining enrolled in accordance with a family care plan established pursuant to paragraph (3) or selecting one of the options specified in subparagraphs (B) and (C) of paragraph (4).

paragraph.text: Nothing in this section shall be construed as requiring or providing for the changing of admission requirements at any of the covered service academies.

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term covered service academy means the following:

subparagraph.text: The United States Military Academy, West Point, New York.
The United States Naval Academy, Annapolis, Maryland.
The United States Air Force Academy, Colorado Springs, Colorado.
The United States Coast Guard Academy, New London, Connecticut.
The United States Merchant Marine Academy, Kings Point, New York.

paragraph.text: The term Secretary concerned means—

subparagraph.text: with respect to the United States Military Academy, the United States Naval Academy, and the United States Air Force Academy, the Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Secretaries of the military departments and the Superintendent of each such academy;

with respect to the United States Coast Guard Academy, the Secretary of Homeland Security, in consultation with the Commandant of the Coast Guard and the Superintendent of the Coast Guard Academy; and

with respect to the United States Merchant Marine Academy, the Secretary of Transportation, in consultation with the Administrator of the Maritime Administration and the Superintendent of the Merchant Marine Academy.

section.header: Defense language continuing education program

subsection.text: Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness shall coordinate with the Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency to designate an executive agent for commercially available advanced foreign language training to meet operational readiness requirements of the Department of Defense.
The executive agent designated in subsection (a) shall be responsible for the following:

paragraph.text: Developing policies, procedures, and curricula to allow for continuing language training when linguists transition to operational environments from education or training environments, such as the Defense Language Institute, the Defense Language and National Security Education Office, or service-based training.
Identifying the resourcing requirements necessary for each armed force to have access to the following foreign language training elements:

subparagraph.text: A foreign language and current culture training and maintenance virtual immersion program covering strategic languages (as designated by the Federal Government), with a range of multimedia materials including—

clause.text: current and authentic copyrighted multimedia content (video, audio, print, etc.), in multiple genres, that have been cleared for legal use;
foreign-originated newscasts and interviews with foreign speakers; and

any other content determined by the executive agent to be necessary for personnel to acquire proper vocabulary, phraseology, and enhanced understanding of the nuances associated with foreign cultures.

subparagraph.text: Anytime accessibility, both on-line and via mobile device.
Training programs with success proven by previous partnerships with academic institutions in the United States or other departments and agencies of the Federal Government.

subsection.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the executive agent, in coordination with the chief of each covered Armed Force, shall establish a procedure through which the Armed Force shall reimburse any organization of the Department of Defense that provides instruction under this section to members of that Armed Force for the costs of such instruction.
In this section, the term covered Armed Force means the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Space Force.

section.header: Public-private consortium to improve professional military education

subsection.text: The Secretary of Defense, acting through the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and in consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, may establish and maintain a public-private consortium (referred to in this section as the Consortium) to improve and broaden professional military education for military officers and civilian employees of the Federal Government.

paragraph.text: The President of the National Defense University and the head of a civilian institution of higher education appointed in accordance with paragraph (3) shall serve as co-directors of the Consortium.
The co-directors shall be responsible for—

subparagraph.text: the administration and management of the Consortium; and
developing a common curriculum for professional military education using input received from members of the Consortium.

paragraph.header: Appointment of co-director from civilian institution
paragraph.text: Not later than June 1, 2022, the Secretary of Defense shall appoint an individual who is the President or Chancellor of a civilian institution of higher education to serve as co-director of the Consortium as described in paragraph (1).

The co-director appointed under paragraph (3) shall serve an initial term of five years. The Secretary of Defense may reappoint such co-director for one or more additional terms of not more than five years, as the Secretary determines appropriate.
In the event that a conflict arises between co-directors of the Consortium, the conflict shall be resolved by the Director for Joint Force Development of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (J–7).

subsection.text: The Consortium shall carry out the following activities:

paragraph.text: Bring the military education system (including military service academies, institutions that provide professional military education, and other institutions the provide military education) together with a broad group of civilian institutions of higher education, policy research institutes, and the commercial sector to develop and continually update a research-based curriculum to prepare early career, mid-career, and senior military officers and civilian employees of the Federal Government to succeed in an era that will be predominantly defined by great power competition and in which security challenges will transcend the traditional areas of defense expertise, becoming more complex and inter-related than before, with disruptions that will manifest rapidly and with little warning.
Train military officers and civilian educators serving in the joint professional military education system to implement the curriculum developed under paragraph (2) at the institutions they serve.

On a regular basis, make recommendations to the Secretary about how the joint professional military education system should be modified to meet the challenges of apparent or possible future defense, national security, and international environments.

subsection.text: The Consortium shall be composed of representatives selected by the Secretary of Defense from the following organizations:

paragraph.text: Organizations within the joint professional military education system.
Military service academies.
Other institutions of the Federal Government that provide military education.
Civilian institutions of higher education.
Private sector and government policy research institutes.
Organizations in the commercial sector, including organizations from the industrial, finance, and technology sectors.

subsection.text: Not later than September 30, 2023, and annually thereafter, the co-directors of the Consortium shall submit to the Secretary of Defense and the appropriate congressional committees a report that describes the activities carried out by the Consortium during the preceding year.
In this section:

paragraph.text: The term appropriate congressional committees means—

subparagraph.text: the Committee on Armed Services and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives; and
the Committee on Armed Services and the Committee on the Environment and Public Works of the Senate.

paragraph.text: The term civilian institution of higher education means an institution of higher education (as defined in section 101 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1001)) that is not owned or controlled by the Federal Government.

section.header: Standards for training of surface warfare officers and enlisted members

subsection.text: Not later than September 30, 2022, the Secretary of the Navy shall establish standards and procedures (subject to subsection (b)) by which a Navy surface warfare officer or enlisted member of the Navy who serves in a bridge or engine department may be issued a merchant mariner credential in accordance with part E of subtitle II of title 46, United States Code, including—

paragraph.text: a merchant mariner credential with a national officer endorsement under section 10.109(a) of title 46, Code Federal Regulations, as in effect on the date of the enactment of this Act;
a national rating endorsement under subsection (b) or (c) of section 10.109 of such title; or
a Standards of Training, Certification, and Watchkeeping endorsement under section 10.109 (d) of such title.

subsection.text: In no case shall the standards described in subsection (a) be less stringent than the standards applied by the Army, Military Sealift Command, or Coast Guard vessel operators.

Upon establishment under subsection (a), the Secretary of the Navy shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report that updates the military-to-mariner transition provided in response to section 568 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (Public Law 114–328) that includes—

paragraph.text: a description of the how the training program for surface warfare officers exceeds the minimum requirements for a merchant mariner credential with an appropriate endorsement—

subparagraph.text: meets the requirements for a merchant mariner credential with an appropriate endorsement; and
exceeds such requirements;

paragraph.text: a list of the proposed naval curriculum courses that have been submitted to the National Maritime Center for course credentialing approval; and
a timeline for—

subparagraph.text: all personnel described in subsection (b)(1) to be qualified to be issued merchant mariner credentials with national officer and ratings endorsements; and
50 percent of such personnel to receive such credential with Standards of Training, Certification, and Watchkeeping endorsement.

subsection.text: In this section, the term appropriate congressional committees means the following:

paragraph.text: The congressional defense committees (as that term is defined in section 101 of title 10, United States Code).
The Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives.
The Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate.

section.header: Professional military education: report; definition

paragraph.text: Not later than July 1, 2022, the Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a report setting forth the results of a review and assessment of the definition of professional military education in the Department of Defense and the military departments as specified in subsection (c).
The report under this subsection shall include the following elements:

subparagraph.text: A consolidated summary of all definitions of the term professional military education used in the Department of Defense and the military departments.
A description of how such term is used in the Department of Defense in educational institutions, associated schools, programs, think tanks, research centers, and support activities.
An analysis of how such term—

clause.text: applies to tactical, operational, and strategic settings; and
is linked to mission requirements.

subparagraph.text: An analysis of how professional military education has been applied and linked through all levels of Department of Defense education and training.
The applicability of professional military education to the domains of warfare, including land, air, sea, space, and cyber.
With regards to online and virtual learning in professional military education—

clause.text: an analysis of the use of such learning; and
student satisfaction in comparison to traditional classroom learning.

subsection.text: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the Secretaries of the military departments, using the report under subsection (a), shall standardize the definition of professional military education across the military departments and the Department of Defense.

section.header: Study on training and education of members of the Armed Forces regarding social reform and unhealthy behaviors

subsection.text: Not later than April 1, 2022, the Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Secretaries of the military departments, shall conduct a study on training and courses of education offered to covered members regarding—

paragraph.text: sexual assault;
sexual harassment;
extremism;
domestic violence;
diversity, equity, and inclusion;
military equal opportunity;
suicide prevention; and
substance abuse.

subsection.text: The study under subsection (a) shall identify, with regard to each training or course of education, the following:

paragraph.text: Sponsor.
Location.
Method.
Frequency.
Number of covered members who have participated.
Legislation, regulation, instruction, or guidance that requires such training or course (if applicable).
Metrics of—

subparagraph.text: performance;
effectiveness; and
data collection.

paragraph.text: Responsibilities of the Secretary of Defense or Secretary of a military department to—

subparagraph.text: communicate with non-departmental entities;
process feedback from trainers, trainees, and such entities;
connect such training or course to tactical, operational, and strategic goals; and
connect such training or course to other training regarding social reform and unhealthy behavior.

paragraph.text: Analyses of—

subparagraph.text: whether the metrics described in paragraph (7) are standardized across the military departments;
mechanisms used to engage non-departmental entities to assist in the development of such training or courses;
incentives used to ensure the effectiveness of such training or courses;
how each training or courses is intended to change behavior; and
costs of such training and courses.

paragraph.text: Recommendations of the Secretary of Defense to improve such training or courses, including the estimated costs to implement such improvements.
Any other information the Secretary of Defense determines relevant.

subsection.text: Not later than July 1, 2022, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a report on the results of the study under this section.
In this section, the term covered member means a member of an Armed Force under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of a military department.

subtitle.header: Military Family Readiness and Dependents’ Education

section.header: Establishment of Exceptional Family Member Program Advisory Council

subsection.text: Chapter 7 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting before section 187 the following new section 186:

section.header: Exceptional Family Member Program Advisory Council

subsection.text: There is an Exceptional Family Member Program Advisory Council in the Department of Defense (in this section referred to as the Council).

The Council shall provide, to the Secretary and the chiefs of the covered armed forces, recommendations regarding how to improve the Exceptional Family Member Program. The Council shall provide such recommendations not less than once every six months.
The Council shall be composed of the following:

paragraph.text: One member of each covered armed force—

subparagraph.text: serving on active duty;
who has a dependent—

clause.text: enrolled in the Exceptional Family Member Program; and
with an individualized education program; and

subparagraph.text: appointed by the Vice Chief of Staff of the covered armed force concerned.

paragraph.text: Two military spouses—

subparagraph.text: of members eligible to be appointed under paragraph (1);
who are not civilian employees of the Department of Defense;
one of whom is married to an enlisted member and one of whom is married to an officer; and
appointed by the Vice Chief of Staff of the covered armed force concerned.

paragraph.text: One adult dependent—

subparagraph.text: enrolled in the Exceptional Family Member Program; and
appointed by the Vice Chief of Staff of the covered armed force concerned.

paragraph.text: One representative of the Exceptional Family Member Program Coalition.
One member of the Defense Health Agency.
One member of the Department of Defense Education Activity.
One member of the Office of Special Needs.

subsection.text: In making appointments under subsection (c), the Vice Chief of Staff of the covered armed force concerned shall seek to represent the diversity of the disability community.

Each member of the Council shall serve a term of two years, except one of the original members appointed under subsection (c)(2), selected by the Secretary of Defense at the time of appointment, one shall be appointed for a term of three years.
The Council shall meet at least once every calendar quarter, in person or by teleconference.
In this section, the term covered armed force means an armed force under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of a military department.

paragraph.text: The table of sections at the beginning of such chapter is amended by inserting before the item relating to section 187 the following new item:

toc.toc-entry: 186. Exceptional Family Member Program Advisory Council.

paragraph.header: Termination of advisory panel on community support for military families with special needs
paragraph.text: Section 563 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Public Law 111–84; 10 U.S.C. 1781c note) is amended by striking subsection (d).

section.header: Non-medical counseling services for military families
section.text: Section 1781 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:

paragraph.text: In carrying out its duties under subsection (b), the Office may coordinate programs and activities for the provision of non-medical counseling services to military families through the Department of Defense Family Readiness System.

Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a mental health care provider described in paragraph (3) may provide non-medical counseling services at any location in a State, the District of Columbia, or a territory or possession of the United States, without regard to where the provider or recipient of such services is located, if the provision of such services is within the scope of the authorized Federal duties of the provider.
A mental health care provider described in this subsection is a person who is—

subparagraph.text: a currently licensed mental health care provider who holds a license that is—

clause.text: issued by a State, the District of Columbia, or a territory or possession of the United States; and
recognized by the Secretary of Defense;

subparagraph.text: a member of the armed forces, a civilian employee of the Department of Defense, or a contractor designated by the Secretary; and
performing authorized duties for the Department of Defense under a program or activity referred to in paragraph (1).

paragraph.text: In this subsection, the term non-medical counseling services means mental health care services that are non-clinical, short-term and solution focused, and address topics related to personal growth, development, and positive functioning.

section.header: Expansion of support programs for special operations forces personnel and immediate family members

subsection.text: Section 1788a(e) of title 10, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.text: in paragraph (4), by striking covered personnel and inserting covered individuals; and
in paragraph (5)—

subparagraph.text: by striking covered personnel and inserting covered individuals;
in subparagraph (B), by striking and at the end;
in subparagraph (C), by striking the period at the end and inserting ; and; and
by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:
immediate family members of individuals described in subparagraphs (A) or (B) in a case in which such individual died—

clause.text: as a direct result of armed conflict;
while engaged in hazardous service;
in the performance of duty under conditions simulating war; or
through an instrumentality of war.

section.header: Clarification of qualifications for attorneys who provide legal services to families enrolled in the Exceptional Family Member Program
section.text: Section 582(b)(7) of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (Public Law 116–283) is amended, in the matter preceding subparagraph (A), by striking in education law and inserting and with experience in the practice of education law in the State in which the military installation is located (and any other State or States in which a significant portion of the personnel assigned to such military installation reside).

section.header: Improvements to the Exceptional Family Member Program

subsection.header: Verification of suitability of housing and educational institutions
subsection.text: Section 582(c)(2) of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (Public Law 116–283) is amended by inserting , and to verify that housing and at least one school near such military installation is suitable for the dependent with special needs of such covered member before the period at the end.

subsection.header: Expansion of advisory panel on community support for military families with special needs
subsection.text: Section 563(d)(2) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Public Law 111–84; 10 U.S.C. 1781c note) is amended—

paragraph.text: by striking seven and inserting nine;
by inserting , appointed by the Secretary of Defense, after individuals;
by inserting each before a member;
by striking the second sentence; and
by adding One such individual shall be the spouse of an enlisted member and one such individual shall be the spouse of an officer in a grade below O-6. at the end.

subsection.text: The Secretary of the military department concerned shall, if such Secretary determines it feasible, permit a covered member who receives permanent change of station orders to elect, not later than 14 days after such receipt, from at least two locations that provide support for the dependent of such covered member with a special need.

The Secretary of a military department shall require that a DD Form 2792 completed by a covered member is scanned and uploaded to the electronic health record of the dependent described in such DD Form 2792.
In this section, the term covered member means a member of an Armed Force—

paragraph.text: under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of a military department; and
with a dependent with a special need.

section.header: Database of next of kin of deceased members of the Armed Forces
section.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall prescribe regulations that establish and maintain a database of the Department of Defense that contains up-to-date contact information for the next of kin of members of the Armed Forces under the jurisdiction of the Secretaries of the military departments. Such regulations shall ensure that—

paragraph.text: a commander in a grade higher than O-5 may access the contact information for the next of kin of a member who died while a member of the unit under the command of such commander, regardless of whether such member served under such commander; and
an individual named in such database may—

subparagraph.text: elect to not be contacted by an officer described in paragraph (1); and
change such election at any time.

section.header: Policy regarding remote military installations

subsection.text: Not later than April 1, 2022, the Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Secretaries of the military departments, shall develop a uniform policy for how to—

paragraph.text: identify remote military installations; and
assess and manage challenges associated with remote military installations.

subsection.text: The policy under subsection (a) shall address the following:

paragraph.text: Activities and facilities for the morale, welfare, and recreation of members of the Armed Forces.
Availability of housing, located on and off remote military installations.
Educational services for dependents of members of the Armed Forces, located on and off remote military installations.
Availability of health care.
Employment opportunities for military spouses.
Risks associated with having insufficient support services for members of the Armed Forces and their dependents.

subsection.text: Not later than July 1, 2022, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a report setting forth—

paragraph.text: the policy under this section; and
an implementation plan for the policy.

subsection.text: In this section, the term military installation has the meaning given that term in section 2801 of title 10, United States Code.

section.header: Feasibility study on program for drop-in child care furnished to certain military spouses at military child development centers

subsection.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall conduct a feasibility study on the establishment of a program under which the military spouse of a covered member may leave a covered child with a child care employee—

paragraph.text: at the military child development center of the military installation that is the permanent duty station of such covered member;
during the normal hours of operation of the military child development center at which such child care employee is employed; and
for not more than two hours per week.

subsection.text: Not later than September 30, 2022, the Secretary shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a report regarding the results of the study under subsection (a).
In this section:

paragraph.text: The terms child care employee and military child development center have the meanings given such terms in section 1800 of title 10, United States Code.
The term covered child means the dependent child of a covered member—

subparagraph.text: younger than seven years of age; and
who does not regularly receive child care services at a military child development center.

paragraph.text: The term covered member means a member of the Armed Forces performing active duty for a period of more than 30 days at a location other than the permanent duty station of such member.

section.header: Comptroller General of the United States reports on employment discrimination against military spouses by civilian employers
section.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and 180 days thereafter, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on employment discrimination against military spouses by civilian employers, including on the basis of military spouse status. Such report shall include an assessment of the following:

paragraph.text: The feasibility of policy solutions to prevent such discrimination, including—

subparagraph.text: by amending the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act of 1994 (Public Law 103–353) to ensure that military spouses are covered under such Act; and
by including military spouses as a protected class for the purpose of laws relating to employment discrimination.

paragraph.text: Potential differential effects of such discrimination across race and gender, to determine if military spouses who are people of color are subject to intersectional discrimination.

section.header: Report on efforts of commanders of military installations to connect military families with local entities that provide services to military families
section.text: Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a report on how and the extent to which commanders of military installations connect military families with local nonprofit and government entities that provide services to military families, including assistance with housing.

section.header: Report on Preservation of the Force and Family Program of United States Special Operations Command

subsection.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Commander of United States Special Operations Command shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on POTFF.
The report under this section shall include the following:

paragraph.text: An assessment of the human performance domain of current programs and activities, including—

subparagraph.text: physical conditioning;
exercise physiology;
kinesiology;
nutrition guidance;
rehabilitative support (including physical therapy); and
mental skills training (including sports psychology).

paragraph.text: A description of efforts of the Commander to assess the unique needs of members of special operations forces, including women and minorities.
An assessment of the effectiveness of POTFF in addressing such unique needs.
Plans of the Commander to improve POTFF to better address such unique needs.

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term POTFF means the Preservation of the Force and Family Program of United States Special Operations Command under section 1788a of title 10, United States Code.
The term special operations forces means the forces described in section 167(j) of title 10, United States Code.

section.header: GAO review of Preservation of the Force and Family Program of United States Special Operations Command

subsection.text: Not later than April 1, 2022, the Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a review of POTFF and submit to the appropriate committees a report containing the results of such review.
The report under this section shall include the following:

paragraph.text: An assessment of the sufficiency of the human performance domain of current programs and activities of POTFF.
A description of efforts of the Commander of United States Special Operations Command to assess the unique needs of members of special operations forces, including women and minorities.
A description of plans of the Commander to improve POTFF to better address the unique needs of members of special operations forces.
Changes in costs to the United States to operate POTFF since implementation.
Rates of participation in POTFF, including—

subparagraph.text: the number of individuals who participate;
frequency of use by such individuals; and
geographic locations where such individuals participate.

paragraph.text: Methods by which data on POTFF is collected and analyzed.

Outcomes used to determine the effects of POTFF on members of special operations forces and their immediate family members, including a description of the effectiveness of POTFF in addressing unique needs of such individuals.

subsection.text: Not later than January 31, 2022, the Comptroller General shall provide to the appropriate committees a briefing on the preliminary findings of the Comptroller General under the review under this section.
In this section:

paragraph.text: The term appropriate committees means the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives.
The term POTFF means the Preservation of the Force and Family Program of United States Special Operations Command under section 1788a of title 10, United States Code.
The term special operations forces means the forces described in section 167(j) of title 10, United States Code.

section.header: Continued assistance to schools with significant numbers of military dependent students

subsection.header: Assistance to schools with significant numbers of military dependent students
subsection.text: Of the amount authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2022 in division D of this Act and available for operation and maintenance for Defense-wide activities as specified in the funding table in section 4301 of this Act, $50,000,000 shall be available only for the purpose of providing assistance to local educational agencies under subsection (a) of section 572 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2006 (Public Law 109–163; 20 U.S.C. 7703b).

subsection.header: Impact aid for children with severe disabilities
subsection.text: Of the amount authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2022 in division D of this Act and available for operation and maintenance for Defense-wide activities as specified in the funding table in section 4301 of this Act, $20,000,000 shall be available for payments under section 363 of the Floyd D. Spence National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2001 (Public Law 106–398; 20 U.S.C. 7703a).
In this section, the term local educational agency has the meaning given that term in section 7013(9) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 7713(9)).

section.header: Verification of reporting of eligible federally connected children for purposes of Federal impact aid programs

subsection.text: On an annual basis, each commander of a military installation under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of a military department shall submit to such Secretary a written certification verifying whether the commander has confirmed the information contained in all impact aid source check forms received from local educational agencies as of the date of such certification.

Not later June 30 of each year, each Secretary of a military department shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report, based on the information received under subsection (a), that identifies—

paragraph.text: each military installation under the jurisdiction of such Secretary that has confirmed the information contained in all impact aid source check forms received from local educational agencies as of the date of the report; and
each military installation that has not confirmed the information contained in such forms as of such date.

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: Term congressional defense committees has the meaning given that term in section 101(a)(16) of title 10, United States Code.

The term impact aid source check form means a form submitted to a military installation by a local educational agency to confirm the number and identity of children eligible to be counted for purposes of the Federal impact aid program under section 7003(a) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 7703(a)).
The term local educational agency has the meaning given that term in section 8101 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 7801).

section.header: Information on female and minority participation in military service academies and the Senior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps
section.text: Section 113 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (c)(2), by inserting before the semicolon the following: , including the status of diversity and inclusion in the military service academies and the Senior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps programs of such department;
in subsection (l)(2)—

in subparagraph (E), by inserting , attendance at military service academies, and enrollment in the Senior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps that before is representative; and

paragraph.text: in subsection (m)—

subparagraph.text: by redesignating paragraphs (5) through (7) as paragraphs (6) through (8), respectively; and
by inserting after paragraph (4) the following new paragraph:

paragraph.text: The number of cadets and midshipmen from the Senior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps of each armed force who are expected to be commissioned into the armed forces during the fiscal year covered by such report, disaggregated by gender, race, and ethnicity.

section.header: Surveys on diversity, equity, and inclusion and annual reports on sexual assaults and racial and ethnic demographics in the military justice system

subsection.header: Modification of content of certain surveys

paragraph.text: Section 481 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
